newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina studies overhaul of tax regime.
newsitem.headline: Argentina studies overhaul of tax regime.

text.p: The Argentine government is considering creating a new, broader income tax and eliminating employer and wealth taxes, Finance Secretary Pablo Guidotti was quoted as saying Wednesday.
The tax overhaul would seek to increase the tax base and reduce employer's costs to foster job creation, Guidotti told the daily La Nacion newspaper in an interview.

"We will analyze the possibility of unifying some taxes, such as employers, income and wealth tax, all in one. That would eliminate taxes on labor and bring income tax more in line with international standards," Guidotti said.
The government collects around $6.0 billion a year in income tax which equals two percent of GDP. The government wants to raise that to 10 percent of GDP, Guidotti said.
The project will be discussed with International Monetary Fund officials in April when a mission is scheduled to visit Argentina to monitor the country's fiscal situation.
